rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_ambix/plot_style.py hides the style-sheet application, the named colour roles and the direct-label helper behind the roles plus one apply function, and figures_jt60sa_geometry.py hides "phase store to drawable families" behind one reader that §2 reuses rather than re-reading the store.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the design routes root resolution through the catalogue owner (load_packaged_machine_map → description_store_root_path), channel addressing through eddb, and geometry reading through imas.DBEntry, the sanctioned IMAS reader; it names the two inline palettes in scripts/figures/*.py and scopes restyling them out, and the phase-directory join uses the catalogue's own declared map name rather than a second placement resolver, so no shared mechanism (placement, path resolution, scheduler query, state reader) is forked.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 adds one new module (imas_ambix/plot_style.py) and states in its own text that it is the first and retires nothing, with the reason (no plotting style code in the repository), and §2/§3 add only figure scripts and PNG/SVG artifacts, none of which touch a counted family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched data/, gs/ and scripts/ and every mechanism it cites exists and does what it says: paths.py owns JT60SA_ROOT/JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR, eddb.py owns channel_path/channel_time_path/UNIT_ATTR, machine_map.py owns load_packaged_machine_map/MachineMapCatalog.description_store_root_path, and read_geometry_table in description_reader.py does return the adapted table (geometry_table_from_description), so declining it for evidence figures is correct; catalog.maps carries the phase name (jt60sa-description-op1) that the static-over-map addressing joins.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the new module is the repository's first plotting-style surface (no style module, mplstyle loader or colour-role table exists in imas_ambix/ or scripts/), so there is no existing mechanism to extend, and §1 states this ("first and retires nothing: imas_ambix/ holds no plotting style code") rather than wrapping an existing one.
